It's worth noting that WoW is a bit of an anomaly as far as MMOs go. While many MMOs yield a ~20% female playerbase, WoW fields a much higher proportion, yielding an average of More than a third of its playerbase, with higher numbers being on RP servers, and lower numbers on Latin American/Brazilian servers (take of what what you will). Additionally, many male players will play female characters, and vice versa, so until someone talks on voice chat or brings up their sex (which is pretty uncommon), you have no way of telling whether it's a guy or girl on the other side of the screen (although there are trends, such as males playing tanks or melee DPS, or female Tauren more commonly being played by middle-aged women).

With that said, WoW has become a much less social game in general over the years, so it's not just you in that case. Similarly, coming across weirdos is nothing new. Know what? They probably would have asked you the same thing, even if you were actually a guy playing a female character.

In short, the WoW community is hardly sexist against female players (unless you have an exceptionally broad definition of "sexism").
